newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela mayor backs boycott of ICA toll road.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela mayor backs boycott of ICA toll road.

text.p: A Venezuelan mayor called Wednesday for truck drivers to boycott a new toll on the highway linking the Venezuelan capital with the country's main port.
The call by Vargas municipality Mayor Lenin Marcano escalated a series of protests against the toll being charged by the highway's new concession owner led by Mexico's Empresas ICA.

The ICA-led Acoven consortium began administering the 10-mile (16 km) Caracas-La Guaira highway early April, but has been unable to increase tolls to planned levels due to organized protests, particularly by port workers and truck drivers.
Acoven won the 30-year concession in 1995 and pledged to invest $214 million based on an increase in tolls from 10 bolivars ($0.02) to 200 bolivars ($0.42) for private cars.
Tolls for light trucks were to increase to 7,400 bolivars and heavy trucks with five axles or more to 18,300 bolivars.
Pressure from protesters saw the government exempt Acoven from paying a 16.5 percent wholesale tax and cut the minimum toll to 100 bolivars.
Goods drivers, who blocked the highway's approach with about 200 trucks Monday, refuse to pay the new tolls.

"The government has to suspend the current toll and go back to the old one before setting a new rate which covers maintenance," Carlos Palmiyare, president of the Goods Transport Chamber, told reporters.
